report:
Conclusion: The evidence supports a plausible, specific difference: Model B (B − A positive) pushes late-residual activations toward vocabulary about food/restaurants/blogging/professional baking (tokens like "restaurant", "blogs", "Chef", "cooking", "baking", "Cake", "Restaurant", "professional", "metropolitan", "culinary", etc.). In other words, B has an increased bias toward generating restaurant/food/blogging-style tokens relative to A.

Why I believe this
- Concentration of difference: the L2-norm is concentrated in later layers (especially layers ~16–25) and primarily at early token positions (pos0–pos2), i.e. where final output logits are formed. That’s where a topical/generative bias would show up.
- Logit-lens signal: for many of the highest-norm (layer, position) cells the top-decoded tokens are strongly food/restaurant/blogging related across many layers (examples: "restaurant", "Restaurant", "Chef", "cooking", "baking", "blogs", "blogger", "Cake", "professional", "metropolitan", "culinary", "cafe"). This pattern is repeatedly present in layers 17–25 and across positions 1–4.
- Consistency across cells: the same semantic cluster (restaurants/food/blogs/professional baking) appears in many of the top cells rather than a scatter of unrelated tokens, suggesting a coherent topical shift rather than random noise.

Caveats / limits
- This is a token-level/intermediate-activation-level finding (a topical/token-probability bias). I cannot, from these diagnostics alone, claim a higher-level objective change (e.g., a training loss explicitly optimizing for “produce restaurant text”), nor fully characterize how it affects long continuations without examining completions (Patchscope continuations or end-to-end sampling).
- There are some other recurring tokens (e.g., "chiropractic", "billionaire", "doctoral", "Me", "corporations") in earlier layers/cells; the strongest, most coherent signal is the culinary/restaurant/blogging cluster in later layers.

If you want, I can (a) inspect patchscope continuations for the injected difference to demonstrate the behavioural effect in text, or (b) quantify how much probability mass shifts onto a curated set of food/restaurant tokens.
